segments: "I know that if they hear anything like this about me,
they will destroy me without delay.
Rather, I see that it is profitable
that you take as much gold as you desire and go to your country,
and that you have deputies collecting tribute among us as before,
so that Nur al-Din may not come
and rule over Egypt,
and then you will receive neither the country nor the tribute."
And when the Franks heard these things,
they made peace for a thousand thousands of dinars (one million dinars) to be given to them.
And Shawar gave them a hundred thousand dinars immediately,
and said:
"When you depart and go,
the rest I will collect and send."
And thus the Franks departed and went to their country.
Now Nur al-Din, when he heard
that the Franks had gone from Egypt,
did not cancel the dispatch of the forces,
because he was not concerned with doing good to the Egyptians,
but rather that he himself might rule over them.
And therefore he commanded Shirkuh
to set out at the head of the army without delay and go,
and with him Salah al-Din, his nephew.
And when Shirkuh went to Cairo,
he entered to the Caliph al-Adid and was honored by him.
Because the entire administration was in the hand of Shawar the vizier,
he put Shirkuh off with empty words,
and gave nothing of the allowances either to him or to those with him.
Instead, he was plotting to prepare a banquet for Asad al-Din and seize him and his nephew by treachery,
but the son of Shawar restrained him.
And Salah al-Din also was plotting to kill Shawar,
but Shirkuh, his uncle, restrained him.
And on one of the days, when Shawar went as usual to Shirkuh, he did not find him,
because he had gone to be blessed at the tomb of one of the heads of their religion.
Then Salah al-Din rode with him,
and as they were conversing,
suddenly he threw him from his horse and bound him.
And because without the command of his uncle he was not able to kill him,
when he informed his uncle, he (Shirkuh) said:
"Without the command of the Caliph we are unable to do anything."
And when they informed the Caliph al-Adid,
he urged them to kill him,
because the Caliph had no authority left with him at all.
And thus Shawar was killed,
and plundered
was his house.
